By Augusta Saraiva and Andrew RosatiOctober 25, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTCBookmark

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wasn’t going down without a fight. And his fans weren’t ready to give up on him. Here, marching down Sao Paulo’s most iconic avenue, they were bearing witness to what may turn out to be the last rally by the most defining figure of Latin America’s left.
On Saturday, hours before Brazilians head to the polls to choose their next leader, the 80-year-old president drew hundreds of thousands to show up for him. It was a sea of red-clad supporters that were chanting, dancing and raising their hands in the air to form the letter L, all for a man who’s been at the center of the nation’s politics for the past four decades.

Singapore expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city-state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies.
The National Environment Agency sent notices seeking documents and details of land concessions in Indonesia owned by the firms, their fire-fighting and blaze prevention measures, and their relationship to other relevant companies, according to a Friday statement.

Saudi Arabia’s main airport was gearing up to reopen as early as Sunday after operations had been disrupted by a spate of attacks by Houthi rebels.
King Khalid International Airport said in a post on X that Terminal 1 will be used for domestic flights and Terminal 2 will be for international flights, but passengers should check with airlines before heading to the airport.

It was a panicked message from a colleague that woke fund manager Ivelina Green at 5 a.m. on Thursday morning in New York: “Total meltdown.”
The average risk premium for US high-yield debt had climbed to a 17-month high and primary markets notched the year’s biggest spate of pulled deals. In London, Arini Capital Management, one of the biggest hedge fund investors in the high-yield market, just told investors it had lost 6.9% in the first half of October.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Metals traders are earning billions of dollars in a second consecutive blowout year for the sector, with several top trading houses notching up record profits.
Trafigura Group, which competes with Glencore Plc for the title of the world’s largest metals trader, made a record profit of around $2 billion in metals trading in its financial year that ended in September, according to people familiar with the matter. Glencore, too, has been enjoying some of its best-ever profits, although its overall results have been marred by a $480 million provision related to its exposure to iron ore trader Radiant World.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A Chinese engineering company is on the cusp of partially restarting a massive Venezuelan power plant that’s been largely idle for years, a crucial step toward fixing the nation’s dilapidated grid.
China Machinery Engineering Corp. plans to switch on a 600-megawatt, oil-fired unit next month at the sprawling Planta Centro complex, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the matter isn’t public. The company is working on the plant under a contract dating back to the presidency of the late Hugo Chávez.

item.description: Dalmore Capital is among parties that have expressed interest in acquiring UK commercial equipment supplier and services provider JLA Group from buyout firm Cinven, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: How This County Made the Data Center Boom Pay Off
item.description: AI is driving a wave of new data centers, but communities are increasingly asking what they get in return. Virginia’s Loudoun County turned the industry into a major tax base that helped fund schools, parks and infrastructure, yet even there, officials are now putting limits on further growth. The bigger lesson may be that towns have more bargaining power than they think. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indonesia Begins Trimming Pipeline Gas Exports to Singapore
item.description: Indonesia is reducing natural gas exports to neighboring Singapore as President Prabowo Subianto seeks to shore up domestic supply and strengthen energy security for Southeast Asia’s largest economy.

item.title: Inside Gershkovich’s 16 Months in Russian Prisons
item.description: Wall Street Journal foreign correspondent Evan Gershkovich tells Bloomberg This Weekend how his reporting experience and knowledge of Russia helped him understand that his 2023 arrest on false espionage charges was likely intended to make him part of a prisoner exchange. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gershkovich discusses his 16 months in Russian prisons, his memoir This Cursed Beautiful Land and what Stephen Hubbard’s release says about Moscow’s use of detained Americans in its dealings with Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)
